elements.evidence: "Corio may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience at any time"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall refund to Corio ... any prepaid fees allocable to the period after such effective date"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience."
"upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice" (30 days, not 60–90)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "without penalty, early termination charge or other liability" (no fee at all)

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience." (no end-of-term/90-day mechanic; more customer-favourable)

reasons: The inserted 11.1A supplies every preferred atomic element: Customer (Corio) convenience right, 30 days' prior written notice, refund of prepaid fees allocable to the post-termination period, and an express bar on Vendor (Commerce One) convenience termination.
The locked target level (preferred) is fully satisfied; the fallback is a separate, unmet bargain (30 days rather than 60–90 days), which is irrelevant because preferred is met.

The clause was absent from the original, so a single concise inserted paragraph is the minimal fix; no existing sentence (11.1 term/renewal, 11.2 breach and insolvency termination, Warranty Period condition) was altered.

Ancillary phrases ('in whole or in part', 'without penalty ... or other liability', 30-day refund payment window) are short mechanics that operationalise the fee-free pro-rata refund and favour our party; they introduce no undefined term, contradiction or dangling mechanic.
The deterministic check flagging absence of a Customer convenience termination is not borne out by the rendered operative text, which expressly grants Corio that right.
